tool_args.rationale: The initial rows show saturation with current input, while the targeted open-branch observations show a strong monotone gradient modulation in the opposite direction. Fit a compact saturating-in-input law with an exponential gradient factor and offset numerically; this captures the observed branch effect without claiming that the underidentified two-hop dynamics have been resolved.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The existing seven rows already span the saturating input response and include two deliberately varied gradient values, enough to test a compact gradient-modulated law; a larger trajectory batch is not justified yet.
This is explicitly nuisance information and does not resolve the input/gradient dependence.

The bridge/flux signatures motivate this mechanism, but the available observations provide only one horizon and do not independently identify compartment rates; a simpler fitted saturating response is more economical at this stage.

considered_alternatives.option: Beverton-Holt recruitment with no gradient dependence
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: It explains the fixed-gradient saturation but cannot account for the large systematic response changes at gradients 0.2 and 2.3.
